mainEntity.name: How long do direct composite restorations last on incisal edges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Direct composite restorations on incisal edges typically last 5-10 years with proper care. Longevity depends on factors including the extent of wear, bite forces, oral hygiene, and dietary habits. Regular dental check-ups allow for monitoring and early intervention if repairs become necessary. Patients with bruxism may experience shorter restoration lifespans unless protective night guards are used consistently.

mainEntity.name: Is the direct composite restoration procedure painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many patients report minimal discomfort during direct composite restoration for incisal edge wear. Local anaesthetic is often unnecessary since the procedure typically involves minimal tooth preparation. Some patients may experience slight sensitivity immediately following treatment, which usually resolves within a few days. Post-treatment sensitivity can be managed with over-the-counter pain relief if needed.

mainEntity.name: Can composite restorations be whitened if my teeth change colour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite restoration materials do not respond to tooth whitening treatments in the same way as natural tooth structure. If significant colour changes occur, the composite may need replacement to match newly whitened teeth. Planning any whitening treatment before composite restoration allows for optimal colour matching of the restoration materials to the desired final shade.

mainEntity.name: What foods should I avoid after composite restoration treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the first 24-48 hours following composite restoration, avoid hard, sticky, or heavily pigmented foods that might damage or stain the new restoration. This includes nuts, hard sweets, coffee, red wine, and berries. After the initial healing period, normal eating habits can typically resume, though maintaining good dietary practices helps preserve the restoration long-term.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my composite restoration needs repair or replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signs that composite restoration may need attention include visible chips or cracks, rough or sharp edges, colour changes, or increased sensitivity. Changes in bite comfort or food catching around the restoration also warrant professional evaluation. Regular dental examinations allow for early detection of restoration problems before they become more significant.

mainEntity.name: Will my bite feel different after incisal edge restoration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Initially, restored teeth may feel slightly different when biting or speaking. This is normal as you adjust to the restored tooth shape. Most patients adapt quickly, though some may require minor adjustments to achieve optimal comfort. If bite irregularities persist beyond a few days, contact your dentist for evaluation and possible adjustment.
